_comment: B=8 specialization of the N=512-K=192 file. This is MLA q_nope -> W_K
absorption for a 64-head model at TP=8 (GLM-5.3: kv_lora_rank 512,
qk_nope_head_dim 192, 64/8 = 8 local heads).
The (N, K)-only file is tuned at a larger B and picks BLOCK_SIZE_M 64 x
BLOCK_SIZE_N 256 for 32 <= M <= 256. The grid is
(B, cdiv(M, BM) * cdiv(N, BN)), so at B=8 that is 8 * 2 * 2 = 32
workgroups on a 256-CU gfx950 -- 12.5 % of the device, on a GEMM whose
0.79 MB of weights put its HBM floor near 0.25 us. Every tile below was
measured bit-identical to the shipped one (max abs diff 0.00e+00); this
file only changes how the same work is spread.
Measured by graph replay on MI355X, us per call, best tile vs shipped:
The M=48/80/96 rows are worst because 64 does not divide them, so the
shipped tile also loses the EVEN_MN fast path on top of the starved grid.
M >= 1536 keeps the shipped large-M tile: at M=2048..11588 the grid is
already full and nothing measured beat it by more than run-to-run noise.
M <= 24 keeps the shipped small-M tiles, which were already best there.
bench_mla_bmm_config.py in the GLM-5.3 tree regenerates the whole table.
